BOM groups repeated components with their values and LED colour; jumper rows show endpoints, wire colour, user-entered measured length when available, and geometric minimum separation otherwise. The minimum is not a cut-length recommendation; assembly slack and bends must be measured.

Browser-local page library creates, opens, auto-saves, duplicates, deletes, and exports up to 100 independently named board projects; an older single saved project is imported into the library on first use and retained as a legacy backup. These are independent projects, not multi-sheet electrical connectivity.

Browser-local action summaries track component placement, removal, movement and edits plus jumper placement, removal, endpoint changes and colour changes; rapid edits coalesce; history is capped at 300 entries, viewable by project name, and exportable as JSON. Project contents are not copied into the audit log.

Advisory checks report mixed declared signal domains, multiple active outputs on one net, non-overlapping explicitly declared terminal voltage ranges, and input-only nets. Missing pin limits stay unknown; this is not a standards or safety approval.

Missing equipment tags are assigned by device family, cable routes receive stable project-local CBL tags, and circuit references link board/protection/RCD IDs with cable tags in schedules. Verify local designation conventions before issue; no standards compliance is implied.

Material schedule groups placed quantities by floor and specification, calculates orthogonal route lengths with declared runs/spare, and labels cross-floor routes unmeasured until surveyed rise is supplied. Catalogue identity does not establish procurement suitability.

Floor selector navigates storeys; rooms/devices are assigned per floor, drawings render only the active floor, and project recovery preserves the hierarchy. Validation rejects active-floor and object-floor references outside the declared storeys.
Device-local drawing audit records project-level add/remove/edit counts without embedding drawing contents; the visible history is capped at 300 entries and coalesces rapid edits

Wall-mode routes follow connected wall geometry, avoid door/window openings at the declared routing height, validate endpoints and orthogonal geometry, and warn when equipment lacks a room assignment; manual routes remain explicitly reviewable
